[[Brokerage firm]] | assets = $196.7 billion (2015){{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/global2000/list/4/#header:assets_sortreverse:true|title=The World's Largest Public Companies|website=[[Forbes]] }} | subsidiaries = DC Advisory | website = {{url|http://www.daiwa-grp.jp/english/}} }} {{nihongo|'''Daiwa Securities Group Inc.'''|大和証券グループ本社|Daiwa Shōken Gurūpu Honsha}} is a Japanese [[investment bank]] that is the second largest [[brokerage firm|securities brokerage]] after [[Nomura Securities]].{{Cite web|title=Japan's top three brokerages to pare grad hiring as households shun stocks|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2017/04/11/business/japans-top-three-brokerages-pare-grad-hiring-households-shun-stocks/|date=2017-04-11|website=The Japan Times|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-28}} Major subsidiaries include ''Daiwa Securities'', which offers retail services such as [[online trading]] to individual investors and investment banking services in Japan, as well as ''Daiwa Capital Markets'', the firm's international investment banking arm (with a presence across Asia, Europe and North America) that provides [[Mergers and Acquisitions|M&A]] advisory, sales and trading services in a variety of financial products to corporate and institutional clients. Other group companies provide [[asset management]], research and [[private equity fund]] services. The company is the fourth largest shareholder in [[SL Green Realty]].{{cite news|last1=Putzier|first1=Konrad|title=Who Will Be Holding the Bag?|url=http://therealdeal.com/issues_articles/who-will-be-holding-the-bag/|access-date=3 September 2015|publisher=The Real Deal|date=1 September 2015}} ==History== ===Daiwa Securities SB Capital Markets=== The company was founded in 1999 as Daiwa Securities SB Capital Markets Co. Ltd., a joint venture between Daiwa Securities Group (Daiwa) and Sumitomo Bank (SB). It was renamed in 2001 to Daiwa Securities SMBC Co. Ltd., after Sumitomo Bank merged with Sakura Bank on 1 April 2001 to form Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG). However, in 2010, SMBC acquired Nikko Cordial (Japan's third-largest brokerage at that time). ===Daiwa Securities Capital Markets Company=== Following this step, Daiwa dissolved the joint-venture with SMBC and re-acquired 100% of the shares in the company, before renaming it again as Daiwa Securities Capital Markets Co. Ltd. Finally, about two years later, the company was absorbed in a merger, leaving Daiwa Securities Co. Ltd as the sole entity.{{Cite web |title=Daiwa Securities Co. Ltd. and Daiwa Securities Capital Markets Co. Ltd. entering into a Merger Agreement|publisher=Daiwa Securities Group |url=https://www.daiwa-grp.jp/data/current/press-3129-attachment.pdf |access-date=16 Oct 2025}} === DC Advisory === In May 2009, Daiwa acquired the [[corporate finance]] division of [[Close Brothers Group]]. In 2010, it was renamed to DC Advisory and now acts as the corporate finance arm of Daiwa.{{Cite web |last=Vaughan |first=Liam |date=26 April 2011 |title=DC Advisory Partners shrugs off false start |url=https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/dc-advisory-shrugs-off-false-start-20110425 |website=Financial News}} ==Member companies== * Daiwa Financial Holdings Co., Ltd. * Daiwa Securities Co., Ltd. * Daiwa Asset Management Co., Ltd. * Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd. * Daiwa SB Investments Ltd. * Daiwa Securities Business Center Co., Ltd. * The Daiwa Property Co. Ltd. * Daiwa Capital Markets America Inc. * Daiwa Capital Markets Europe Ltd.{{Cite web|url=https://www.daiwa-grp.jp/english/about/group/|title=Group Companies | About Daiwa Securities Group}} ==Projects== In July 2012, Daiwa Securities Group was chosen by the [[Central Bank of Myanmar]] to spearhead a $380-million project designed to develop an IT network for the Myanmar government that would connect all ministries as well as schools and hospitals to a cloud computing system and would also entail a secure online banking system for the country.{{Cite news | title = Is Myanmar a business opportunity bonanza? | publisher = Investvine.com | date = 2013-01-15 | url = http://investvine.com/is-myanmar-a-business-opportunity-bonanza/ | access-date = 2013-02-03 | archive-date = 5 March 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130305041630/http://investvine.com/is-myanmar-a-business-opportunity-bonanza/ | url-status = dead | first=Justin |last=Calderon }} In December 2024, Daiwa Securities announced its aims to raise wages by 5% to attract new talents to its company. The initiative is expected to begin by April, 2025.{{Cite news |date=December 23, 2024 |title=Japan's Daiwa aims to raise wages at least 5% next year to attract talent |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/japans-daiwa-aims-raise-wages-least-5-next-year-attract-talent-2024-12-23/}} ==See also== *[[Daiwa Anglo-Japanese Foundation]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Daiwa Securities Group}} * {{Official website|http://www.daiwa-grp.jp/index.cfm}} {{in lang|ja}} * [http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/Daiwa-Securities-Group-Inc-Company-History.html Fundinguniverse.com Company History] * {{cite web|url=http://www.nccjapan.net/shashiwiki/index.php?title=Daiwa_Shoken_Gurupu_Honsha|title=Company history books (Shashi)|publisher=Shashi Interest Group|date=April 2016}} Wiki collection of bibliographic works on Daiwa Securities Group {{TOPIX 100}} {{Nikkei 225}} {{Investment banks}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Daiwa Securities Group| ]] [[Category:Financial services companies based in Tokyo]] [[Category:Primary dealers]] [[Category:Financial services companies established in 1943]] [[Category:Banks established in 1943]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies in the Nikkei 225]] [[Category:Japanese companies established in 1943]]
extract:
Daiwa Securities Group Inc. (大和証券グループ本社, Daiwa Shōken Gurūpu Honsha) is a Japanese investment bank that is the second largest securities brokerage after Nomura Securities.
Major subsidiaries include Daiwa Securities, which offers retail services such as online trading to individual investors and investment banking services in Japan, as well as Daiwa Capital Markets, the firm's international investment banking arm (with a presence across Asia, Europe and North America) that provides M&A advisory, sales and trading services in a variety of financial products to corporate and institutional clients. Other group companies provide asset management, research and private equity fund services.
The company is the fourth largest shareholder in SL Green Realty.
